title: What makes a substance an acid or an alkali
examples: What is the difference between a base and an alkali?
Is soap an acid or an alkali?

explain.say: Why does lemon juice taste sharp, while soap feels slippery? They sit at opposite ends of a big chemistry family. Look at the board. You can see things from your home sorted into three groups.

draw.text: What makes a substance an acid or an alkali

explain.say: See the acids? Lemon juice, vinegar, cola, even the acid in your stomach. Acids taste sour, but never taste anything in a lab, as strong ones burn! What do you think all acids have in common?

Look at the board. When an acid dissolves in water, it releases hydrogen ions, written H plus. An ion is a particle with a charge, and these ones make the water acidic. Can you guess what an alkali releases?

explain.say: Hydroxide ions, written OH minus! Look at the second reason. Alkalis, like soap and oven cleaner, give out OH minus ions in water. Strong alkalis are as dangerous as strong acids. Have you noticed how slippery soapy hands feel?

explain.say: Great work! Look at the alkali group. A base is anything that cancels out an acid, and an alkali is a base that dissolves in water. Wow: your stomach makes hydrochloric acid, the same acid used in school labs, and a slimy lining stops it hurting you.

faq.q: What makes a substance an acid?
faq.a: An acid releases hydrogen ions, H plus, when it dissolves in water. The more hydrogen ions, the more acidic the solution.
An alkali is a base that dissolves in water and releases hydroxide ions, OH minus. Sodium hydroxide and soap solutions are alkalis.
asks: What is the difference between a base and an alkali?

faq.a: Strong alkalis, like oven cleaner and drain cleaner, are corrosive and can burn skin and eyes as badly as strong acids. Always wear eye protection.
Sour foods contain acids, like citric acid in lemons and limes, ethanoic acid in vinegar, and lactic acid in yoghurt.

faq.q: How can you test if something is an acid?
faq.a: Use an indicator. Litmus turns red in acid and blue in alkali, and universal indicator shows a colour for each pH.
asks: How do you test for an acid?

facts: Acids produce hydrogen ions (H+) in water; alkalis produce hydroxide ions (OH-).
The stomach makes hydrochloric acid, giving stomach juice a pH of about 1.5 to 3.5.
